note: mise v2026.6.14 on one Windows 11 PC, all toolchain state isolated to a tmp MISE_DATA_DIR. Two flavors of evidence: a behavioral matrix (what mise did in each scenario) and a small set of timings. Timings are a 2026-06-29 snapshot; the durable claims are the behaviors, not the milliseconds. mise ships ~monthly so versions have since moved.

behavioral_matrix.description: Each row is one scenario run against mise v2026.6.14 with an isolated MISE_DATA_DIR. 'observed' is what actually happened; 'meaning' is the durable claim.

rows.observed: An untrusted mise.toml with an [env] block made `mise env` REFUSE to parse: 'Config files ... are not trusted. Trust them with `mise trust`.' After `mise trust`, the [env] block loaded.
rows.meaning: TOFU (trust-on-first-use) security model: a cloned repo's config cannot silently inject PATH/env. Trust is an explicit gate before any config-driven mutation.

rows.observed: Lockfile is OFF by default (no mise.lock auto-created). After setting lockfile=1 and creating an empty mise.lock, `mise use node@22` wrote per-platform sha256 + download URL for every (os,arch) target into mise.lock.
rows.meaning: Reproducibility unit is a cross-platform BINARY checksum, not a version string. A Windows dev and a Linux CI resolve the same lock to their own verified, identical-by-hash binary. But it is OFF unless you opt in.

rows.observed: On `mise install` the standalone exe printed 'mise-shim.exe not found ... falling back to "file" shim mode'. shims/.mode = 'file'. Each shim is a bash script + a .cmd twin whose body is `mise x -- node %*`.
rows.meaning: The standalone exe does not bundle the compiled mise-shim.exe, so it falls back to file shims that re-spawn mise every call -> shims only work while mise itself is on PATH. Scoop/winget installs ship the exe shim.

rows.observed: `mise run build` with [tasks.build] depends=["greet"] executed greet -> build in order (95.5 ms total).
rows.meaning: A dependency-aware task runner is built in; no make/Taskfile needed for simple pipelines.

rows.observed: After trust, [env] APP_ENV=firsthand plus _.path=["./bin"] made `mise env` export APP_ENV and prepend ./bin to PATH.
rows.meaning: direnv-style directory-scoped env + PATH shaping, gated behind the same trust model as T.

rows.observed: `mise use aqua:jqlang/jq@1.7.1` downloaded the release sha256sum.txt and verified the checksum. No cosign / no attestation step.
rows.meaning: jq's aqua config is checksum-only: it guarantees the bytes match the published checksum, but the checksum ships FROM THE SAME RELEASE, so a fully-compromised upstream could publish a matching bad pair. Integrity, not provenance.

rows.observed: `mise use aqua:cli/cli@2.62.0` ran [1] download, [2] verify GitHub artifact attestations (success, queried via mise-versions.jdx.dev/api/github/repos/cli/cli/attestations/sha256:...), [3] checksum, [4] extract.
rows.meaning: Tools with an attestation config get PROVENANCE (who built it, how) verified, which is stronger than checksum-only. Caveat: the attestation lookup goes through mise's OWN API, so you trade some trust to mise's infrastructure.

rows.observed: Both mise.jdx.dev (200) and mise.en.dev (200) respond. The v2026.6.14 binary emits mise.en.dev in its trust-error / lockfile comments; the scout-cited canonical is mise.jdx.dev.
rows.meaning: A domain in the tool's own output (mise.en.dev) that differs from the doc canonical (mise.jdx.dev) is real, not a hallucination — both resolve. Noted so the post's URLs are not 'corrected' to a single domain by mistake.

timings.description: Wall time on the one Windows PC. Machine-dependent; the cold-vs-warm shape and the shim delta are the portable signals, not absolute ms.

rows.label: cold install node@22
rows.note: Single command; installed node v22.23.1 from scratch.

rows.label: warm reinstall node@22 (already installed)
rows.note: Idempotent; re-run cost ~= 0 vs the 3287 ms cold path.

rows.label: raw node.exe invocation
rows.note: Baseline: call the resolved node binary directly.

rows.label: mise exec -- node invocation
rows.note: file-shim path re-spawns `mise x`; ~+14 ms per call over raw.

findings.claim: An untrusted mise.toml is refused at parse time until `mise trust`.
findings.detail: Because config can rewrite PATH/env, mise gates it behind trust-on-first-use. `mise env` on an untrusted config errors ('Config files ... are not trusted') instead of silently loading it. This blocks a freshly-cloned repo from injecting env the instant you cd into it.

findings.claim: mise.lock pins cross-platform binary checksums, not just version strings — and it is OFF by default.
findings.detail: With lockfile=1 and an existing mise.lock, `mise use node@22` records sha256 + URL for each (os,arch). Two machines on different OSes resolve the same lock to their own hash-verified, identical binary. Forget to enable it and you get 'same version, possibly different binary'.

findings.claim: The standalone mise.exe falls back to 'file' shim mode because mise-shim.exe is absent, so shims depend on mise being on PATH.
findings.detail: The exe shim (compiled mise-shim.exe copied per tool) is the default/recommended mode, but the bare standalone exe does not ship it. File shims (.cmd + bash pair calling `mise x`) re-spawn mise every invocation and break if mise leaves PATH. Scoop/winget installs include mise-shim.exe and use exe mode.

findings.claim: 'mise verifies downloads' means three different things with three different guarantees.
findings.detail: core lockfile sha256 (integrity of a pinned binary) / aqua checksum-only e.g. jq (bytes match a checksum from the same release — integrity, not provenance) / aqua attestation e.g. gh (GitHub build provenance verified, stronger — but the lookup routes through mise's own API). Do not read 'verified' as uniform.

findings.claim: Reinstalling an already-installed tool is near-free.
findings.detail: Warm `mise use node@22` = 110 ms vs 3287 ms cold, so putting `mise install` in a shell hook / CI step is cheap on the common path.

findings.claim: The file-shim adds a small per-call cost.
findings.detail: raw node.exe 76 ms vs `mise exec -- node` 90 ms (~+14 ms) from the `mise x` re-spawn. Negligible for interactive use, worth knowing for tight inner loops that shell out per iteration.

explicitly_not_verified.note: The exe shim mode (via Scoop/winget with mise-shim.exe present) was NOT run here — only the file-shim fallback of the standalone exe was measured. The exe-mode behavior is described from mise docs, cited not measured.
Everything was measured on Windows 11 only. macOS/Linux activate (shell hook) mode, which the post mentions as more capable there, was not measured on this run.

The checksum-only vs attestation guarantee difference is reasoned from what each backend verifies; no actual upstream-compromise attack was staged. It is a threat-model argument, not an exploited PoC.
